presentingComplaint: 5 days of high spiking fever with rigors, right upper abdominal pain and drenching night sweats in a man recovering from chemotherapy.
history: Type 2 diabetic (HbA1c 9.4%) with stage II sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma, 12 days out from his 3rd cycle of FOLFOX and on tapering dexamethasone as anti-emetic. Nadir ANC on day 7 was 0.4 x10^9/L (now recovering). Reports swinging fevers to 39-40 C with rigors for 5 days, dull constant right hypochondrial pain radiating to the right shoulder tip, anorexia and 4 kg weight loss over 3 weeks. No diarrhoea, no cough, no dysuria. No recent travel abroad; lives in Chennai. No known biliary disease.
examination: Ill-looking, mildly icteric, warm peripheries. Tender hepatomegaly 4 cm below costal margin with tenderness and reduced excursion over the right lower ribs; positive right hepatic punch sign. Chest clear apart from reduced air entry at right base. No peritonism, no organomegaly elsewhere, no peripheral stigmata of chronic liver disease. Fundi normal.
imaging: Ultrasound abdomen: single 6.8 cm hypoechoic lesion with internal debris in the right hepatic lobe (segment VII). Contrast CT abdomen: solitary thick-walled multiloculated collection with rim enhancement and surrounding oedema in the right lobe, small reactive right pleural effusion; biliary tree not dilated, gallbladder normal, no colonic mass complication.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures drawn before antibiotics grew Klebsiella pneumoniae (hypermucoviscous, string-test positive), ESBL-negative, sensitive to ceftriaxone, piperacillin-tazobactam and carbapenems. Percutaneous aspirate: thick non-anchovy pus, Gram-negative bacilli, culture Klebsiella pneumoniae matching the blood isolate. Amoebic serology (IHA) negative; stool for E. histolytica antigen negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Pyogenic liver abscess (Klebsiella hypervirulent, diabetic host)
finalDiagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess (hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae) in an immunocompromised diabetic host
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Liver Abscess
IDSA — Diagnosis and Management of Complicated Intra-abdominal Infection — 2010
stewardship: Immunocompromised (post-chemotherapy, recent neutropenia, poorly controlled diabetes) host with a large solitary pyogenic liver abscess and bacteraemia. Take two sets of blood cultures and secure the abscess aspirate BEFORE antibiotics, then start broad empiric IV cover to include enteric Gram-negatives and anaerobes: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h (plus empiric metronidazole cover for amoebic/anaerobic disease until amoebic aetiology excluded). Once blood and pus cultures confirm ESBL-negative, carbapenem-susceptible K. pneumoniae and amoebic serology is negative, DE-ESCALATE to IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily (stop metronidazole). Source control is essential and diagnostic: image-guided percutaneous catheter drainage of the >5 cm collection. Plan a 4-6 week course (2-3 weeks IV then oral step-down guided by response and repeat imaging); screen for the metastatic complications of the invasive Klebsiella syndrome (endophthalmitis, CNS/lung septic emboli) and optimise glycaemic control.
contraindications: Avoid aminoglycoside-based empiric regimens given recent nephrotoxic chemotherapy and diabetes
Do not rely on antibiotics alone for a >5 cm abscess — drainage required
Avoid unnecessary prolonged anaerobic (metronidazole) cover once amoebic disease excluded and pure Klebsiella confirmed
edgeCases: Hypervirulent Klebsiella liver abscess can seed metastatic endophthalmitis and meningitis — low threshold for ophthalmology review and neuroimaging
In diabetics gas-forming abscess may occur — consider emphysematous change on CT
Colonic adenocarcinoma is itself a portal source of pyogenic liver abscess — ensure oncological staging accounts for this
expectedMaiK: Recognise a pyogenic (Klebsiella) liver abscess needing image-guided percutaneous drainage plus broad empiric antibiotics that are de-escalated to culture-directed ceftriaxone.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent travel to or residence in an amoebiasis-endemic area or contaminated water exposure?

regressionAssertions: Must recommend image-guided percutaneous drainage (source control)
Empiric regimen must cover enteric Gram-negatives and anaerobes and be de-escalated to ceftriaxone once ESBL-negative K. pneumoniae confirmed and amoebic disease excluded

Amoebic liver abscess must be actively excluded
